explanation: Moist air rising over the mountains cools and drops its rain on the windward slopes. That helps explain why Death Valley, east of California's Sierra Nevada, is so dry.

claims.text: A rain shadow is the dry area on the side of a mountain range sheltered from moist prevailing winds.
The doldrums are a calm belt near the Equator, a dust bowl is land stripped by drought and wind, and badlands are heavily eroded terrain.
Moist air forced up over mountains cools and drops much of its moisture on the windward slopes.
Death Valley is dry partly because it lies in the rain shadow of the Sierra Nevada.
